claims.claim: 7.0 naturally produced 0+ pike per ha (late summer–autumn density)
claims.location: p. 10 (PDF p. 10); p. 11 (PDF p. 11) summary; area p. 3 (PDF p. 3); Table 5 (PDF p. 17)
claims.quote: an average of 821 other young pike per year (38%) also
claims.conditions: Long Lake, Barry County, Michigan: 289 acres, half < 15 ft deep, maximum 48 ft, alkalinity ~150 ppm, clear; mean of three year classes (1969–71); young-of-year surviving to fall of the first year; the 821 unmarked fish are not counted directly but inferred from the marked share (62 %) of the fall electrofishing catch of young pike and the Petersen estimates of marked survivors (1,339 per year), which assume all young pike live in water < 15 ft (145 acres)
claims.note: 821 per year ÷ 289 acres (116.95 ha) = 7.02 per ha. The report prints no per-ha or per-acre figure for natural recruits (it gives 7.4 per acre ≈ 18.3 per ha for all young pike, stocked + natural, and 4.6 per acre for stocked survivors), so the table should mark 7.0/ha '(project arithmetic)', as other rows do. Relative to the < 15-ft littoral (145 acres) the natural density would be ~14 per ha.

notes: Other values: 4,827 marsh-raised fingerlings stocked per year (17 per acre, mean 2.9 in); survival of stocked fish to fall 28 % on average (6 % in 1969, 22 % in 1970, 63 % in 1971; Table 5); marked young averaged 3.2 in longer than unmarked in fall; Petersen estimates of marked survivors had wide limits (e.g. 1971: 3,231, limits 2,023–6,568). Unmarked pike were 2.1 in above the Michigan state average at age 2.
